english.notes:
(i) This offence applies from 4am on 5th January 2023.
(ii) Please note - whilst this is a summary offence, the offence is not governed by the 6 month time limit that would usually apply to offences as set out in section 127(1) of the Magistrates Court Act 1980. This is because the offence is created by regulations made under the Public Health (Control of Disease) Act 1984. Section 64A of the Public Health (Control of Disease) Act 1984 provides the time limits for this offence, being before the end of the period of 6 months beginning with the date on which evidence which the prosecutor thinks is sufficient to justify the proceedings comes to the prosecutor's knowledge; and within 3 years of the date of the commission of the offence.
(iii) A pre-departure test means a test for the detection of SARS-CoV-2 that complies with Regulation 4.
(iv) See regulation 3(2) for a list of reasonable excuses for not possessing valid notification of a negative test result.
(v) The Schedule to these regulations provides a list of persons to which this offence does not apply.
(vi) This offence applies to flights arriving in England from mainland China, except from the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and the Macao Special Administrative Region.
(vii) Proceedings for this offence may be brought by the Crown Prosecution Service and any person designated by the Secretary of State (see regulation 10).
(viii) Regulation 9(5) deals with the issue of FPN’s for this offence and specifies that the first fixed penalty is £500. Furthermore, regulation 9(5) also provides that a second fixed penalty notice issued is £1,000; in the case of the third and subsequent fixed penalty notices received, double the amount specified in the last fixed penalty notice received by that person, to a maximum of £4,000.
